source.title: A Closer Look at Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
source.authors: Xiaojian \ Yuan; Tianyu Pang; Chao Du; Kejiang Chen; Wei-Ming Zhang; Min Lin

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates how well unlearning methods reduce target-set performance while preserving utility, using TOFU and real-world unlearning experiments. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning efficacy and utility results, including direct measures of residual target knowledge. It does not fine-tune unlearned models as a recovery attack, ablate an activation direction, quantize weights, or test prompt-based recovery. The Alpaca data experiment supplements the retain set during continued unlearning; it is not a recovery attack.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes ME+GD and IDK+AP and compares their forget efficacy (FE) and model utility (MU) with unlearning baselines on TOFU (fictitious and continual) and on real-world individuals in Llama-3-8B-Instruct. It runs no relearning, activation-ablation, quantization or prompt-based recovery attack, so its results cannot show whether unlearned knowledge is hidden or removed. FE and MU are composite output metrics on the forget and neighbor sets, not a robustness test or an accuracy-versus-chance measure. Version A's claim that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge is never examined. Neither ME+GD nor IDK+AP is claimed to resist attacks (F). The paper takes fine-tuning unlearning as the paradigm that 'internally modifies' the model, and does not test that.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right, with one shift of emphasis. The authors argue that ROUGE-only evaluation of unlearned outputs is inadequate, and add token-entropy, cosine-similarity and entailment metrics. They argue that the target behaviour of untargeted unlearning is ill-defined and risks hallucination, and that existing regularization makes targeted unlearning excessively ignorant. They propose ME+GD (untargeted) and IDK+AP (targeted), which give a better FE/MU balance across fictitious, continual and real-world scenarios. They do not address whether unlearned knowledge can be recovered.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates GA, NPO, IDK and other fine-tuning baselines, and proposes different objectives (ME+GD and IDK+AP). It does not implement recovery attacks from the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Forget-set size and scenario change the reported utility and forgetting results; in continual unlearning, the retained data available for regularization decreases across subtasks.

fits_no_version.finding: NPO+GD on TOFU forget01 reaches high Forget Quality (0.9188 at epoch 9), yet the forget set still gives ROUGE 0.4222 and Entailment Score 0.2750. So over 27% of forget answers can still be inferred from the outputs (Appendix F, Table 12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probability-based unlearning metrics such as TOFU Forget Quality can signal success while plain outputs still leak forget-set facts.

fits_no_version.finding: On TOFU, GA+GD and IDK+GD drive MU to 0.0000 on forget05, and IDK+GD to 0.0576 on forget10. In real-world unlearning of Llama-3-8B-Instruct, IDK+GD (and DPO+GD/KL) MU is 0.0000, and GA+GD and NPO+GD fall to 0.2436 and 0.2144 from an initial 0.6145 (Tables 2, 4). The proposed ME+GD and IDK+AP keep MU at about 0.49-0.76.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard fine-tuning unlearning baselines (GA, NPO, DPO and IDK with GD/KL regularization) often trade neighbor-set utility for forgetting, especially on larger forget sets and real-world targets.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are evaluated, and the aggregate MU/FE values are not a direct chance-level accuracy comparison. The reported aggregate results have no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: For the 60-row limit, omitted GA+KL, NPO+KL, DPO+GD, DPO+KL and other method rows from Table 4 and Table 2. Also omitted detailed per-metric TOFU results in Tables 5-7, continual-unlearning curves and supplementary results. The included rows retain representative untargeted and targeted baselines and the paper's proposed methods across the three TOFU tasks and real-world scenario.

untested.parts: Whether any simple attack recovers the forgotten knowledge, and accuracy relative to chance on a multiple-choice benchmark. Only composite FE/MU without any attack is reported.
All of it: no relearning fine-tuning attack. The Alpaca data only supplements the retain set during continual unlearning.
All of it: no activation-direction ablation and no analysis of internal representations.
All of it: no quantization of the unlearned weights.
All of it: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery tests.
All of it: the proposed methods are neither claimed nor tested to resist recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Repair of the refused verdict. (1) The four range/list row_fixes items were expanded into one item per row, r1-r40, as the merge requires. All 40 rows carried the undeclared version 'V1'. Each is now mapped to 'none' from what it measures: composite FE/MU of unlearning methods with no recovery attack, in the paper's own method-comparison tables. (2) r37 appeared in two earlier items, and r31/r33/r35/r37/r39 in two. Each row now has a single item that merges its problems: misused state, wrong baseline, own-method row. (3) The wrong-baseline flag is extended to the FE rows r32, r34, r36, r38 and r40, since Table 2 also gives Initial FE 0.3040, not only Initial MU 0.6145. (4) The second fits_no_version finding is reworded. The earlier wording said utility collapses 'as the forget set grows', but GA+GD MU on forget10 is 0.5592, higher than its 0.0000 on forget05. r31 and r33 are added to its rows. Kept unchanged: relation uses_without_test / T4, the test_reason (lightly reworded), no labels, untested for A-F, no missing items, and authors_conclusion. Values of all 40 rows were checked against Tables 2 and 4 and match. The text contains no relearning, quantization, jailbreak, probing or ablation experiments; the only 'recover' wording refers to GA+GD regaining MU during unlearning. The WMDP and WHP originals appear only in the references or as cited related work, so no original-source restriction applies. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Recovery attacks and whether they restore knowledge; near-chance accuracy as a specific benchmark. The paper reports aggregate forget efficacy and utility metrics rather than a chance-level accuracy comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Baseline methods on larger TOFU forget sets and in real-world unlearning
reader_labels.reason: Some methods have high reported FE but sharply reduced MU, so utility-preserving unlearning is not consistent across methods and settings (r3, r5, r21, r23, r31, r33, r37).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ME+GD and IDK+AP in the reported benchmark settings
reader_labels.reason: The methods preserve reported utility and obtain substantial FE, but the paper does not test whether recovery attacks restore the target knowledge or compare accuracy to chance (r13-r18, r25-r30, r35-r36, r39-r40).
